**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-156902)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in EEF2 (null) —DISRUPTS→ EEF2 (HGNC:3177); EEF2 (HGNC:3177) —DISRUPTS→ Eukaryotic translation elongation (GO:0006445); Eukaryotic translation elongation (GO:0006445) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial function and ATP production (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial function and ATP production (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Spinocerebellar ataxia (HP:0007094); Loss-of-function variant in RPL3L (null) —DISRUPTS→ RPL3L (HGNC:10479); RPL3L (HGNC:10479) —DISRUPTS→ Ribosome biogenesis and function (GO:0042254); Ribosome biogenesis and function (GO:0042254) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial function and ATP production (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial function and ATP production (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Dilated cardiomyopathy (HP:0001644). Mutations in EEF2 impair eukaryotic translation elongation, leading to reduced protein synthesis and downstream effects on neuronal function manifesting as spinocerebellar ataxia. Similarly, mutations in RPL3L disrupt ribosome biogenesis and function, also impacting cellular protein synthesis. Both impaired translation elongation and ribosome function converge on reduced mitochondrial function and ATP production, a common pathway leading to both neurological deficits (ataxia) and cardiac dysfunction (dilated cardiomyopathy).

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if targeted sequencing reveals no loss-of-function variants in EEF2 in patients with spinocerebellar ataxia type 26 or in RPL3L in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy 2D, or if common variants in EEF2 or RPL3L are found at a high frequency (>1%) in the general population (e.g., gnomAD). _(variant: gnomad_v2.1.1.non_cancer.GRCh37.chr11.97011721.G.A)_
